title: Release sprint gatekeeper criteria and cross-team launch checklist for API / Console / Runtime
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Purpose: Define actionable gatekeeper criteria and a compact cross-team checklist for the upcoming release sprint that covers API, Console, and Runtime surface areas. This ticket captures milestones, cut/roll-forward criteria, release notes coordination plan, and the communication matrix needed to synchronize Product, Eng, Design, QA, Docs, and Support during the sprint. Goal is to minimize last-minute scope churn, ensure release notes accuracy, and provide clear rollback/fallback triggers for high-risk items.
milestones: M1 - Feature freeze candidate list published (2026-02-05) - owners: PMs for each area
M2 - Technical readiness pass (engineering sign-off on performance, SLOs, migrations) (2026-02-12) - owners: ENG leads
M3 - Docs & Release notes draft complete (2026-02-18) - owners: Docs + PM
M4 - Final QA & smoke tests + canary plan locked (2026-02-22) - owners: QA + Eng
M5 - Cut window & release decision meeting (2026-02-24) - stakeholders: PM, Eng, Design, Security, Support
M6 - Release day checklist & communications sent (2026-02-28)
cut_criteria: Severity threshold: Any change that increases 95th percentile latency by >10% versus baseline for production-like load = candidate for cut or targeted rollback
Reliability threshold: Introduces a consumer-visible error class or doubles error rate for a route (>=2x from baseline) = block until mitigations in place
Security/compliance: Any outstanding security review items or incomplete KMS/HSM gating = automatic cut
Data migrations: Any migration without tested rollback and dry-run validated in staging = cut
Documentation: Features shipping with public API surface must have at minimum reference + quickstart snippets in draft = block if missing
Cut decision authority: Release decision requires PM + Eng lead + SRE + Security concurrence; unresolved disputes escalate to Head of Product for tie-break
gatekeeper_matrix: Green: All automated integration tests pass; perf regressions <5%; no open Sev2+ incidents; release notes drafted; security sign-off obtained
Yellow: Non-blocking regressions, documentation gaps flagged, minor perf regressions (5–10%) with mitigation plan; proceed with guarded canary and increased monitoring
Red: Any failing progress against cut criteria above, open security items, or unresolved consumer migration blockers — halt rollout and create immediate hotfix/rollback plan
release_notes_coordination: Owner: Emma Zhou (Docs) - maintain single source of truth in Drive: /Drive/Redwood/ReleaseNotes/runtime-1.21/draft.md
Changelog policy: every public API change must include a one-line summary, risk level (low/medium/high), and migration notes (if applicable)
PR integration: link GitHub PRs in the release notes doc; PRs without linked notes are flagged by PM during cut meeting
Customer-facing highlights: PMs to provide up to three customer-impact bullets per product area (API / Console / Runtime)
Internal release brief: include troubleshooting playbook, SLO deltas, and rollback steps — publish to Slack #releases 24h before deploy
communication_plan: D-7: Draft release notes shared with cross-functional reviewers (Docs, Support, Sales, Legal)
D-3: Readout meeting with Support & Solutions to review known regressions and troubleshooting steps
D-1: Final sign-off meeting (15 min) for go/no-go — required attendees: PM, Eng lead, SRE, Security, Docs lead
Release day: release announcements to customers (email + status page update) and internal #releases channel; provide timeline and expected impact
Post-release: 48h monitoring window with daily status check-ins; retrospective scheduled in Cycle +2
dependencies: DES-271 (console header redesign for feature flag)
acceptance_criteria: All M1–M5 milestones completed and documented in the release playbook
No open critical security findings; security sign-off captured as comment with artifact link
Release notes final draft linked in ticket and copy provided to Support and Sales
Canary plan validated in staging and smoke tests pass on canary nodes
Rollback procedure documented and dry-run executed by SRE
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Last-minute perf regression discovered during final QA. Mitigation: pre-authorized rollback window and emergency patch lanes with 2-hr SLA for ENG on-call
Risk: Docs lag behind shipping APIs causing customer confusion. Mitigation: freeze merges without release-notes link; assign Docs buddy for each API PR
Risk: Cross-team misalignment on feature parity between Hosted/Dedicated/Private builds. Mitigation: compatibility checklist required at M2 and signoff from Release Owner

post_release_tasks: 24h: confirm telemetry and dashboards green (Latency, Error rate, Throughput)
48h: publish customer-facing release notes and add community blog draft to editorial queue
72h: collect list of regressions and categorize: hotfix / roadmap / accepted degradation
Post-mortem: if Sev1/Sev2 incident occurs, produce incident report within 72 hours and link to ticket
